instructions: Put 5 1/2 cups water, the 1 1/2 cups milk, the 1/2 cup piloncillo and the cinnamon stick in a medium saucepan over high heat. Stir until the piloncillo dissolves and it comes to a boil.
Turn the heat down to medium. Chop the chocolate into small pieces, add it, and stir until it melts.
Turn the heat down to low. Whisk in the 3/4 cup masa harina a little at a time, stirring constantly so it stays smooth.
Keep whisking over low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until it's silky and thick.
Take the pot off the heat and remove the cinnamon stick. Pour into mugs and serve hot.
Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat over low heat, whisking in a splash of water or milk to thin it.
method_notes: No version has 20 ratings, so this leads with King Arthur's champurrado (4.4 from 9), which simmers masa harina with piloncillo and stone-ground chocolate. Mexican Food Journal (4.5 from 4) and Hola Jalapeno blend the masa with water first. King Arthur's amounts are doubled for 4 mugs, with 1 1/2 cups of milk in place of some water as its note allows. Check the chocolate label for nuts and gluten.
